subject: MSA: data protection liability carve-out for trade secrets
messages:
From: Natalie Hughes <natalie.hughes@valenciahealth.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: legal@valenciahealth.com
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MSA: liability for confidentiality / trade secrets (redlines attached)

Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the draft MSA. Our legal team has reviewed and attached a redline (Valencia_MSA_redline_20270612.docx). The key open issue is around the limitation of liability: Valencia needs an explicit carve-out so that breaches resulting in loss or misappropriation of trade secrets (or unauthorized disclosure of highly sensitive PHI) are excluded from Redwood's aggregate cap.

Specifically, we propose: “The liability cap set forth in Section 8 shall not apply to damages arising from (i) unauthorized disclosure or misappropriation of Customer’s trade secrets, or (ii) willful breaches of Customer’s confidential health data protections resulting in regulatory fines.”

We recognize this is material, but given the vertical (healthcare) and the sensitivity of the data we process for certain pilots, it's a hard requirement for Valencia to proceed beyond pilot. Can we set up a 30-minute call early next week to discuss?

Attachments: 1) Valencia_MSA_redline_20270612.docx (redline)

Best,
Natalie Hughes
Senior Counsel — Valencia Health

Thanks Natalie — appreciate the clear summary and the redline.

Looping in Neha (legal) and Dev (sales/solutions) to run the carve-out language against our standard liability posture and the technical mitigations we can commit to. We can do a 30-min sync Tue 10am PT if that works for you — tentative invite to follow.

Two quick notes: (1) we prefer a narrowly tailored carve-out tied to demonstrable compromise of trade secrets (not broad, vague categories), and (2) we typically seek to limit any carve-out for regulatory fines to situations involving Redwood’s willful misconduct or gross negligence.

If you can share the Valenica-specific examples of what you view as trade secret data (a short appendix or schedule is helpful), we can fold that into the redline.

Thanks,

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: MSA: liability for confidentiality / trade secrets (redlines attached)

Team —

Reviewed Valencia’s redline. Below is a proposed compromise we can present that preserves our overall cap while addressing Valencia’s concern in a narrow, contractible way. I added a short explanatory rationale for sales.

Proposed language (to insert as an exception to Section 8):
“Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the Parties agree that the limitations and exclusions of liability set forth in Section 8 shall not apply to direct damages arising from: (a) the unauthorized disclosure or misappropriation of the Customer’s trade secrets where such disclosure/misappropriation results from Redwood’s failure to implement or adhere to the technical and organizational measures expressly identified in Schedule 4 (Trade Secret Protections); or (b) Redwood’s willful misconduct with respect to Customer’s regulated personal health information, to the extent that such willful misconduct directly results in regulatory fines imposed on Customer.”

Rationale / guardrails we should insist on: 
- Require a mutually agreed Schedule 4 that lists categories/examples of Valencia trade secrets (narrow, not exhaustive).
- Trigger for exclusion: demonstrable compromise (forensic report + mutually agreed incident review).
- Capability: we will offer reasonable cooperation on forensic investigation and remediation.
- Carve-out remains limited to direct damages — excludes consequential, incidental, speculative damages beyond direct loss.

If Sales wants to offer an enhanced option (higher cap or escrow) for a premium, we can surface that as a commercial add-on. Otherwise this language gives Valencia contractual recourse while preserving our broader commercial model.

Happy to be on the call with Kim & Dev.

—Neha
Senior Corporate Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA: liability for confidentiality / trade secrets (redlines attached)

Neha — +1 on the proposed language. Two practical points for the call and for the commercial counter: 

1) Schedule 4 needs to be simple. Valencia will push for broad definitions; push back and insist on examples + data locations (e.g., PHI datasets marked as SENSITIVE/TRADE_SECRET in the ingestion schema).
2) We should offer a fixed remediation SLA (forensic timeline, containment steps) and commit to pay reasonable third-party forensic costs up to a defined amount, rather than open-ended indemnity.

Suggested commercial fallback options to present if they insist on no cap impact: 
- Option A (standard): Accept the narrow carve-out language above + Redwood pays forensic costs up to $100k; cap remains unchanged.
- Option B (premium): For an elevated committed spend (or a one-time fee) Redwood will: (i) increase the aggregate cap by $X (negotiated), and (ii) provide prioritized support and a 24/7 incident contact.

This gives Sales something to move with without immediately escalating to executive sign-off.

Rishi
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MSA: liability for confidentiality / trade secrets (redlines attached)

Natalie —

Thanks again for the redline and for being clear about Valencia’s priority on this. We discussed internally and attached a short schedule template (trade_secret_schedule.xlsx) that you can populate with the categories Valencia wants included.

Consolidated position (proposal):
- We can accept a narrowly tailored carve-out as set out by Neha above, conditioned on: (i) a mutually agreed Schedule 4 listing categories/examples of protected trade secret data; and (ii) incident triggers that require a forensic report demonstrating Redwood’s failure to adhere to the specified technical/organizational measures.
- Redwood will cover reasonable third-party forensic costs up to $100,000 per incident where Redwood is found to have failed to implement the specified protections.
- The carve-out applies only to direct damages and does not expand consequential or punitive damages protections in other parts of the MSA.

If that is acceptable, we can take the attached schedule from you, fold it into the redline, and circulate a single-file mark for execution. If you prefer the premium route (Option B) Rishi and I can propose numbers.

Link to single-file redline (preview): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDocLink
DocuSign envelope (prepared, pending Valencia approval): https://app.docusign.com/valencia/Envelope12345

Please let me know whether Valencia can live with the proposed wording and whether you’ll complete the schedule or want the upgraded commercial option.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

summary: External legal asked to exclude trade-secret/confidentiality breaches from liability cap. Internal legal proposed narrow carve-out tied to a mutually agreed schedule and forensic trigger; operations suggested paying forensic costs up to $100k as compromise; sales to present to customer with schedule template and optional premium upgrade.
